pr.title: fix(server): a failed Codex turn no longer traps the queue behind its subagents
pr.body:
When a Codex orchestrator's root turn failed while its native subagents were still running, the thread got stuck. The run stayed `running` with no live provider turn, so nothing could be steered, and every message (the user's included) queued behind it until the subagents finished, which can take an hour. Meanwhile both clients showed "Working · Thinking".

Seen on a real thread. A `thread_send` steer made Codex send `response.interrupt`, the upstream rejected it, and the root turn failed at 15:14. Its `/root/takeover_queue_*` subagents kept working past 16:19, and run 12 never left `running`.

## Fix

- **Codex adapter:** `emitOrDeferRootTerminal` held any non-completed root terminal until native descendants finished. A failed root now emits right away with `childTurnsContinue: true`, because Codex subagents run on their own threads and outlive it. Interrupted roots still wait, since Stop interrupts the whole lineage.
- **RunExecutionService:** a flagged failed terminal settles the run as `failed` without cascade-failing the live children, and keeps ingesting until they report their own terminals. That is the same lifetime a completed root already gives them, so the queue drains and the next message starts a fresh turn.
- **Clients:** `ThreadRunSummary.turnEnded` marks an open run whose provider turn has already ended. Web and mobile no longer show the Thinking row in that state. The Working indicator and Stop are unchanged, because the run is still open.

## Verification

- New regression tests, each confirmed to fail without its fix: the Codex replay (failed root + running subagent), RunExecutionService (no cascade, child completion still ingested), the client-runtime derivation, and the web and mobile Thinking row.
- `CodexAdapterV2`, `RunExecutionService`, and related orchestration suites (background work stop, steering completion, subagent projection, delegated completion, run finalization) pass. Typecheck is clean for server, web, mobile, client-runtime, and provider-core.
- Reproduced in a real web client against an isolated dev instance, with a scripted Codex app-server standing in for the CLI. It spawns a native subagent, then fails the root turn with the same `response.interrupt` rejection when steered. Same steps on both builds: start the turn, steer, then send a follow-up.

| Before (main) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: run stuck on Working and Thinking after the turn failed, with the follow-up queued and Steer disabled](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/2548f3765dc28ca8/before-web.png) | ![After: provider error shown, follow-up answered in a new turn, Reviewer subagent still running](https://gh-file-drop-api-prod-mi5fy3sowv63ufte.pinglabs.workers.dev/f/03794b71aa81fb0b/after-web.png) |

  - **Before (main):** the failed turn is invisible. The thread shows "Working · Thinking" indefinitely, and the follow-up sits in the queue with Steer disabled.
  - **After:** the provider error appears in the timeline, the follow-up runs as a new turn, and the Reviewer subagent keeps running under "Waiting on subagent", where Stop still works.
